question: The engine is a crate of its own (evidence 55) and what it offers a caller is `api`: the commands as calls, family by family, each handing back the report its command prints and saying what it could not do in the words the command says. Can a caller that is no command line ask a stream what it is without knowing its family first, read one report of the checks whichever family the stream is of, and tell the kinds of failure apart, from calls that stand on `api` and move nothing the command line says or writes?
method: Five calls at the root of `oadec-engine`, each a few lines over the call of `api` beside it, written against tests that were seen to fail first. The kind of an error is found by what marks it where it arises: a refusal and a source without a stream are each wrapped in a type of their own (which is why `api` builds its refusals through one function and no longer through `bail!`), and an error nothing marks is `Io` when an `io::Error` is in its chain and `Stream` when none is. The words stay the ones the command line says. Held four ways. (1) `tests/calls.rs` holds each call to the call of `api` it stands on, field for field, over the fixtures, the streams the campaign turned up, an AC-3 stream a recipe writes (no fixture is one) and the E-AC-3 fixture with every syncframe made a dependent substream (frames, none of which decodes), and each kind of error to a case of it. (2) An example of the crate, `calls`, was run over every stream of the corpus beside the command line, and every field of the one report compared with the field of the family's report it is read from, the format a call names with what the command says the stream is, and `clean` with the exit codes. (3) Every mutation that is new or whose text changed was run. (4) The binary of main and of the change over the corpus, the help of every command, and the campaign of damaged streams against the tally of main, as for every change that touches what a command says.
commands: cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --all --check; cargo deny check (both workspaces)
cargo run --release -p oadec-engine --example calls -- <stream>...   (beside `oadec info`, `verify --json`, `oamd`, `emdf` of the same streams)
python tools/old_new.py --old <binary of main> --new <binary of the change> --decode-all <the corpus>

reading: A caller needs to know nothing of a stream before it asks. Over the 143 streams of the corpus the calls name the format the command line names, 25 AC-3, 59 E-AC-3, 5 MLP, 54 TrueHD, and every field of the one report is the field of the family's report it is read from, 2145 comparisons with none that differs. What a call could not do says which of four kinds of thing went wrong, in the line the command line writes. For the command line nothing moved: its reports, its deliveries, its help and the answers of the campaign are what they were. One stream is said differently by a call and by a command, frames none of which decodes: the commands print no report, and the calls hand back an error and not a report with nothing in it. The comparison over the corpus earned its place: it found a damaged MLP stream the calls named TrueHD, which the tests had written down as right. What this does not give: a report of the checks whose every field has a type of its own. `regions`, `census` and `protection` are the values the reports of the families have, as JSON, and the one report is built from what `verify --json` prints.
